validity.recommendation: A person should decide whether this row is the 2015 third section plan, the Power of Siberia 3 Far Eastern route, or the new 800 kilometer Khabarovsk to Amur link.
validity.researcher_notes: A 2015 plan gives a third section of 32 billion cubic meters and 620 kilometers. The energy policy paper gives the Far Eastern route as 10 billion cubic meters. Reports from 2022 describe a new 800 kilometer link. The row mixes these ideas.

fills.researcher_notes: The recorded energy policy paper loads. It describes a Far Eastern route called Power of Siberia 3 at 10 billion cubic meters a year. It does not say the expansion was cancelled or shelved. The value stays and a person should check it.

A February 2015 RIA Novosti report on Gazprom plans describes a third section from Blagoveshchensk to Vladivostok at 32 billion cubic meters a year. It is a 2015 plan, not a built or approved line, so tier is medium.
The same 2015 report gives 620 kilometers for that third section. It is a plan figure, so tier is medium.
The 2015 report presents the third section as a Gazprom plan. It does not use the word operator, so tier is medium.
The 2015 report presents the third section as a Gazprom plan. It states no ownership percentage, so tier is medium.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The recorded status is cancelled. No page cited on the wiki states a cancellation. The 2015 plan and the 2022 reports of a new 800 kilometer Khabarovsk to Amur link both leave the status of this expansion open.
status_reviews.recommendation: Leave Status as recorded and have a person check it.

cross_row_leads.researcher_notes: Worth a search beyond the wiki citations for the Far Eastern route rows. Not searched this pass.
